definition: Area of knowledge or activity to which the software is applied.
non_claim: Research scope; not itself a boundary or adoption unit.

definition: Cohesive problem area classified as core, supporting or generic relative to a strategy.
non_claim: Problem-space division; not automatically a bounded context, team, service or product.

definition: Explicit boundary within which one model and ubiquitous language are defined, internally consistent and applicable.
non_claim: Semantic applicability and translation boundary; may contain many aggregates and libraries and may support multiple products.

definition: Cluster with a root that enforces synchronous invariants and transactional consistency.
non_claim: Consistency boundary inside a bounded context; not an integration, deployment or product boundary.

definition: Named domain operation that belongs to no natural entity or value object.
non_claim: Behavior in a bounded context; not automatically independently adoptable.

definition: Typed selectable behavior needed or offered by a composition.
non_claim: Composition axis; can cross product and implementation graphs without owning all involved meanings.

definition: Versioned reusable semantic or implementation contract with explicit operations, laws, dependencies and decisions.
non_claim: Build/reuse unit; may implement part of one context or serve several contexts through published contracts.

definition: Concrete implementation or operated resource offer that can satisfy a typed requirement after qualification.
non_claim: Implementation/operation axis; does not inherit semantic authority from use.

definition: Governed, independently consumable promise of outcomes to defined users with owned adoption, service, lifecycle, evidence and exit.
non_claim: Adoption and outcome boundary; may compose several bounded contexts, capabilities, libraries and providers.

definition: Commercial or internal package of independently governed products.
non_claim: Packaging only; it does not merge semantic owners or lifecycle identities.

definition: Vertical composition of reusable products, capabilities and domain vocabulary for a class of enterprise needs.
non_claim: Configuration/composition boundary; it must not fork horizontal semantics merely by industry name.
